title: Reducing the risks of brain injury, with Kim Gorgens, PhD

sentences.en: Every year, there are more than 2.8 million traumatic brain injuries in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国，每年有超过280万人遭受创伤性脑损伤。

sentences.en: The risks of brain injury among young athletes, pro football players, and members of the military have made headlines in recent years.
sentences.zh: 近年来，年轻运动员、职业橄榄球运动员以及军人面临的脑损伤风险已成为新闻头条。

sentences.en: But other populations are at increased risk as well, including people in the criminal justice system and domestic violence survivors.
sentences.zh: 但其他群体也面临着更高的风险，包括司法系统中的人员以及家庭暴力幸存者。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk to a neuropsychologist about what researchers are learning about the prevalence of brain injury and how best to prevent and treat it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一位神经心理学家探讨研究人员在脑损伤的普遍性以及如何更好地预防和治疗方面有哪些新发现。

sentences.en: So what constitutes a traumatic brain injury?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟什么是创伤性脑损伤？

sentences.en: How common are TBIs?
sentences.zh: 创伤性脑损伤有多普遍？

sentences.en: What happens to the brain when you get a concussion?
sentences.zh: 当人脑受到震荡时，大脑会发生什么？

sentences.en: What should we be doing to help protect athletes from brain injuries, from youth sports to professional leagues?
sentences.zh: 从青少年体育到职业联赛，我们应该采取什么措施来保护运动员免受脑损伤？

sentences.en: What effective therapies do we have to help people recover from TBI?
sentences.zh: 我们有哪些有效的疗法可以帮助人们从脑损伤中恢复？

sentences.en: And what could we be doing to mitigate the harms of brain injury in often overlooked populations such as domestic violence survivors and prison inmates?
sentences.zh: 对于家庭暴力幸存者和监狱囚犯等常被忽视的群体，我们又能做些什么来减轻脑损伤带来的伤害？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Kim Gorgens, a professor of psychology at the University of Denver, where she teaches psychophysiology, clinical neuropsychology,
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是丹佛大学心理学教授金·戈根斯博士，她在那里教授心理生理学、临床神经心理学，

sentences.en: and the psychology of criminal behavior.
sentences.zh: 以及犯罪行为心理学。

sentences.en: She has worked for decades studying and treating brain injuries in populations, including youth athletes, prison inmates, and survivors of domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，她一直致力于研究和治疗各类人群的脑损伤，包括青少年运动员、监狱囚犯和家庭暴力幸存者。

sentences.en: In addition to her research, clinical work, and teaching, she's an advocate for TBI awareness and helped draft a 2020 concussion law in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 除了研究、临床工作和教学外，她还是脑损伤意识的倡导者，并协助起草了科罗拉多州2020年的脑震荡法案。

sentences.en: She also lectures and speaks frequently to the media about brain injury, and her work has been featured in outlets including U.S.
sentences.zh: 她还经常就脑损伤问题发表演讲并接受媒体采访，她的工作曾被《美国新闻与世界报道》、

sentences.en: News, Newsweek, and Scientific American.
sentences.zh: 《新闻周刊》和《科学美国人》等媒体报道。

sentences.en: Dr. Gorgens, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 戈根斯博士，感谢您今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Kim, it's such a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 金，非常荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I think this is the highlight of the year for me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这对我来说是今年的重头戏。

sentences.en: Wow, that's saying a lot.
sentences.zh: 哇，这话分量可真不轻。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I love that it's the Kim and Kim show.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这是“金与金”节目。

sentences.en: Oh, perfect.
sentences.zh: 哦，太完美了。

sentences.en: Yeah, we worked that out.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我们刚才还商量过这个。

sentences.en: So let's start with a fundamental question, which is what is a traumatic brain injury?
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从一个基本问题开始：什么是创伤性脑损伤？

sentences.en: How do doctors know when somebody has had a TBI, and not just a knock on the head?
sentences.zh: 医生如何判断某人是患有创伤性脑损伤，而不仅仅是头部受到撞击？

sentences.en: This is a great question, and there's really two component parts to the question, as you just asked it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，正如你刚才所问的，这个问题实际上包含两个部分。

sentences.en: A brain injury is any insult to the brain, and that means it includes the whole of the universe of traumatic brain injuries.
sentences.zh: 脑损伤是对大脑的任何损伤，这意味着它涵盖了创伤性脑损伤的整个范畴。

sentences.en: Those are injuries that are caused by the application of some external force or a blow to the head.
sentences.zh: 这些损伤是由某种外力作用或头部受到撞击引起的。

sentences.en: We also talk a lot more recently about blast injuries, so a hyperpressurized wave of air.
sentences.zh: 最近我们还谈论了很多关于爆炸伤的问题，也就是高压空气波造成的损伤。

sentences.en: It also includes all the ways the brain can be damaged by being deprived of oxygen.
sentences.zh: 它还包括大脑因缺氧而受损的所有方式。

sentences.en: We call those anoxic brain injuries, as is the case strangulation, near-lethal overdose with synthetic opiates.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为缺氧性脑损伤，例如勒颈或合成阿片类药物导致的近乎致命的过量服用。

sentences.en: The second part of your question, though, is a much more nuanced one, which is, and how do doctors know when you have one?
sentences.zh: 不过，你问题的第二部分要微妙得多，那就是：医生怎么知道你是否患有脑损伤？

sentences.en: And the reality is, we don't have great gold standard diagnostic tests for brain injury, particularly for mild brain injury.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我们目前还没有针对脑损伤，特别是轻度脑损伤的绝佳黄金标准诊断测试。

sentences.en: At this point, there's one new FDA-approved test, an Abbott test, that is available in some settings, only in emergency rooms,
sentences.zh: 目前，FDA批准了一种新的检测方法，即雅培（Abbott）检测，它在某些环境下可用，但仅限于急诊室，

sentences.en: only in settings with laboratories that are designed to run this teSt.
sentences.zh: 且仅限于配备了专门用于进行此项检测的实验室的环境中。

sentences.en: So, a lot of us in the research space, it's like a gold rush to find some easy, standard way of identifying someone who's had a brain injury so that we can say to that person,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们许多研究人员就像是在淘金，急于找到一种简单、标准的方法来识别脑损伤患者，以便我们能对他们说，

sentences.en: here's how you need to be careful as you recover from brain injury.
sentences.zh: 在脑损伤康复期间，你需要注意这些事项。

sentences.en: In the short term, though, what we're left with is subjective complaints of the person who is injured.
sentences.zh: 然而，在短期内，我们只能依靠受伤者主观的症状陈述。

sentences.en: And, of course, that opens the door for other ways that we minimize symptoms, where the culture of whatever we're doing at the time encourages us to walk it off, for example,
sentences.zh: 当然，这也为我们淡化症状留下了空间，比如在当时所处环境的文化鼓励下，我们会选择硬撑过去，

sentences.en: or where it might be too dangerous to disclose having a brain injury in the case of interpersonal violence.
sentences.zh: 或者在涉及人际暴力的情况下，披露自己脑损伤可能过于危险。

sentences.en: And it makes it really difficult for people who sustain brain injury to feel the validation of the healthcare system,
sentences.zh: 这使得脑损伤患者很难从医疗系统中获得认可，

sentences.en: because there isn't a way to say, well, indeed, you've had a brain injury.
sentences.zh: 因为没有一种方法能确切地说：没错，你确实遭受了脑损伤。

sentences.en: So, diagnostically, any alteration of consciousness is a brain injury.
sentences.zh: 所以，从诊断学上讲，任何意识改变都属于脑损伤。

sentences.en: So, if you struck your head or if you were strangled to unconsciousness, that is a mild brain injury.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你头部受到撞击，或者被勒至失去知觉，那都属于轻度脑损伤。

sentences.en: And determining how long that loss of consciousness was, it may be a more moderate or severe injury,
sentences.zh: 而确定失去知觉的时间长短，可能意味着损伤程度更重或更严重，

sentences.en: but at a minimum, any alteration of consciousness is a mild traumatic brain injury.
sentences.zh: 但至少，任何意识改变都属于轻度创伤性脑损伤。

sentences.en: So, what happens to the brain after a traumatic injury?
sentences.zh: 那么，创伤性损伤后大脑会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, is this something that you can sum up easily, or are all brain injuries different?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这能简单概括吗？还是说所有的脑损伤都不尽相同？

sentences.en: I love that you pointed that out.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你指出了这一点。

sentences.en: And in the brain injury world, Kim, you hear a lot of people, and clinicians especially, say if you've seen one brain injury, you've seen one brain injury.
sentences.zh: 在脑损伤领域，Kim，你会听到很多人，尤其是临床医生说：如果你见过一例脑损伤，那你也就只见过那一例而已。

sentences.en: So, there is something very idiosyncratic about people's responses to brain injury.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们对脑损伤的反应是非常独特的。

sentences.en: But uniformly, across the board, mild injuries are metabolic injuries.
sentences.zh: 但统一来看，轻度损伤在本质上都是代谢性损伤。

sentences.en: They're inflammatory injuries.
sentences.zh: 它们是炎症性损伤。

sentences.en: So, much like an injury anywhere in the body, where the body's response, your immune system's response is to mount an inflammatory response,
sentences.zh: 就像身体任何部位的损伤一样，身体的反应，即免疫系统的反应，是引发炎症反应，

sentences.en: to mobilize tissue repair, and to heal the injury.
sentences.zh: 以调动组织修复并治愈损伤。

sentences.en: That same phenomena happens in the brain.
sentences.zh: 大脑中也会发生同样的现象。

sentences.en: We don't resolve inflammation in the brain as quickly.
sentences.zh: 只是我们大脑中炎症的消退速度没那么快。

sentences.en: And neuroinflammation is associated with all manner of really negative effects, things like mood disturbance, and behavioral discontrol, and cognitive complaints.
sentences.zh: 而神经炎症与各种非常负面的影响有关，比如情绪障碍、行为失控和认知抱怨。

sentences.en: So, the inflammatory aftermath of injury is where the really devastating effects come from.
sentences.zh: 因此，损伤后的炎症后遗症才是真正造成毁灭性影响的根源。

sentences.en: Now, kids sports are an area where we hear a lot about TBIs.
sentences.zh: 现在，青少年体育是我们经常听到创伤性脑损伤（TBI）的一个领域。

sentences.en: Is the problem just football, where young players sustain a lot of head injuries, or are there other sports that are also dangerous when it comes to TBIs?
sentences.zh: 问题仅仅出在橄榄球上吗？年轻球员在那里遭受了大量头部损伤，还是说在涉及TBI时，其他运动也同样危险？

sentences.en: Such a great question.
sentences.zh: 问得太好了。

sentences.en: And I am so struck by how real this is for your listeners who maybe followed the story just this last weekend
sentences.zh: 对于你的听众来说，这件事非常真实，我对此深有感触，他们可能刚刚关注了上周末的新闻，

sentences.en: about the young player in Alabama who died after being taken to the emergency room from the field after sustaining a brain injury.
sentences.zh: 关于阿拉巴马州的一名年轻球员，他在赛场上遭受脑损伤后被送往急诊室，最终不幸去世。

sentences.en: And we don't know a lot about that case.
sentences.zh: 我们对那个案例了解不多。

sentences.en: And thankfully, there are few of them, less than 20 a year, where a young athlete dies really on the field.
sentences.zh: 值得庆幸的是，这类案例很少，每年不到20例，即年轻运动员在赛场上直接死亡的情况。

sentences.en: But when we talk about youth sports, we talk a lot about the kinds of forces that the kids on the field are exposed to, and the way their bodies are exposed to those forces,
sentences.zh: 但当我们谈论青少年体育时，我们谈论很多的是孩子们在场上所承受的各种力量，以及他们的身体承受这些力量的方式，

sentences.en: and the way their brains are exposed to those forces.
sentences.zh: 还有他们的大脑承受这些力量的方式。

sentences.en: And your brain is pretty well-designed.
sentences.zh: 其实你的大脑构造相当精巧。

sentences.en: In fact, the most well-protected structure in the entire body is the central nervous system.
sentences.zh: 事实上，全身保护得最好的结构就是中枢神经系统。

sentences.en: And we're pretty well-designed to withstand lateral impact.
sentences.zh: 而且我们天生就具备很好的抗侧向冲击能力。

sentences.en: So deceleration injuries, where your brain comes into contact with a stationary object, and there is a lateral application of force.
sentences.zh: 减速损伤是指大脑与静止物体发生碰撞，并受到横向作用力的情况。

sentences.en: What the brain withstands very poorly is rotational force.
sentences.zh: 大脑最无法承受的是旋转力。

sentences.en: And rotational force gets conferred where part of the body spins, and that force gets conferred to the brain.
sentences.zh: 当身体某部分发生旋转时，这种旋转力会传递给大脑。

sentences.en: If you think about the risk to kids playing youth sports, it's not so much about lateral impact to their helmet, per se, but it's a way that they get checked in the body,
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到青少年参加体育运动所面临的风险，这本身并不完全在于头盔受到的横向冲击，而在于他们身体被撞击的方式，

sentences.en: and that force gets translated to their head.
sentences.zh: 这种力量会传导到他们的头部。

sentences.en: The risk is especially high to younger athletes, where A, their neck musculature is not as strong
sentences.zh: 对于年轻运动员来说，风险尤其高，因为A，他们的颈部肌肉力量不如

sentences.en: as older, more robust athletes, and B, where the size discrepancy between players is much greater.
sentences.zh: 年长、强壮的运动员，而且B，球员之间的体型差异要大得多。

sentences.en: Some kids have hit puberty, some kids haven't.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子已经进入青春期，有些还没有。

sentences.en: And so the way that those forces get conferred in the brains is rotational, and you see a lot more damage from that rotational force.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些力量传导到大脑的方式是旋转性的，你会看到这种旋转力造成的伤害要严重得多。

sentences.en: Some kinds of sports happen to lend themselves to more rotational injuries in the style of play.
sentences.zh: 有些运动的比赛风格恰好更容易导致旋转性损伤。

sentences.en: So that's body check in football and being tackled.
sentences.zh: 比如橄榄球中的身体冲撞和被擒抱。

sentences.en: It's hockey.
sentences.zh: 还有曲棍球。

sentences.en: But it's also, importantly, in our concussion biomarker study, we realized that we were seeing a lot of divers with cognitive complaints,
sentences.zh: 但同样重要的是，在我们的脑震荡生物标志物研究中，我们意识到我们观察到许多有认知问题的跳水运动员，

sentences.en: and we thought, well, gosh, we hadn't even included them.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，天哪，我们甚至都没把他们包括在内。

sentences.en: They were in our control group originally.
sentences.zh: 他们最初是在我们的对照组里。

sentences.en: But what we realized for divers was hitting the water from higher dive points actually was a lateral impact to the brain.
sentences.zh: 但我们意识到，对于跳水运动员来说，从更高的地方入水实际上是对大脑的一种横向冲击。

sentences.en: So it isn't as simple as tackle sports, but it is most dangerously rotational impact.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像擒抱类运动那么简单，但它最危险的地方在于旋转冲击。

sentences.en: But it's really, at the end of the day, any impact to the brain, the accumulation of those impacts over years and years is associated with poor outcomes.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，任何对大脑的冲击，以及多年来这些冲击的累积，都与不良后果有关。

sentences.en: So that speaks to the question of protective equipment.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了防护装备的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, like you have protective equipment in sports like football, but you can't wear anything protective when you're diving.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，虽然橄榄球等运动有防护装备，但你跳水时没法穿戴任何防护装备。

sentences.en: So is equipment an answer?
sentences.zh: 那么装备是解决办法吗？

sentences.en: Or I mean, what is the answer for these other sports where it's really not so much that somebody has conked you on the head?
sentences.zh: 或者说，对于这些并非因为头部被重击而受伤的其他运动，解决办法是什么？

sentences.en: You're just doing the sport.
sentences.zh: 你只是在进行这项运动而已。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we saw this when the NFL got rid of the checking rules or added checking rules so that
sentences.zh: 当NFL废除冲撞规则或增加冲撞规则时，我们看到了这一点，

sentences.en: you didn't have helmet to helmet spearing and youth football added heads up style of play.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不会有头对头的冲撞，青少年橄榄球也增加了抬头比赛的风格。

sentences.en: This is about 15 years ago now, but where kids were trained not to use their helmets in the course of play, so heads up play.
sentences.zh: 这大约是15年前的事了，当时训练孩子们在比赛中不要使用头盔，也就是抬头比赛。

sentences.en: And it reduced injuries tremendously at the NFL level, but it had no impact whatsoever on the frequency of concussions in youth sports.
sentences.zh: 这在NFL层面极大地减少了伤害，但对青少年体育中脑震荡的发生频率却没有任何影响。

sentences.en: So the answer isn't as simple as equipment or playing differently.
sentences.zh: 所以答案并不像装备或改变比赛方式那么简单。

sentences.en: Certainly, helmets have made a dramatic difference, and there is a whole argument to be made about helmets.
sentences.zh: 当然，头盔确实带来了巨大的改变，关于头盔还有很多值得讨论的地方。

sentences.en: And this conversation plays out at the NCAA level and high school level with women's lacrosse.
sentences.zh: 这种对话在NCAA和高中女子长曲棍球比赛中也一直在进行。

sentences.en: And many of your viewers will know this, but women's lacrosse is not required to be helmeted.
sentences.zh: 你们很多观众可能知道，女子长曲棍球并不强制要求佩戴头盔。

sentences.en: A lot of advocates pushed for it to be helmeted at the NCAA level.
sentences.zh: 许多倡导者在NCAA层面推动强制佩戴头盔。

sentences.en: And a lot of opponents say that helmeting girls playing lacrosse would lead to an increased incidence of brain injuries because the style of play would be different.
sentences.zh: 而许多反对者认为，让打长曲棍球的女孩佩戴头盔会导致脑损伤发生率增加，因为比赛风格会发生改变。

sentences.en: And, you know, I appreciate that there are really two trains of thought there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我很理解这两种截然不同的思路。

sentences.en: There is no question that the injury is sustained by unhelmeted lacrosse players.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，未佩戴头盔的长曲棍球运动员所受的伤害，

sentences.en: Are more severe than they are by helmeted players.
sentences.zh: 比佩戴头盔的运动员更严重。

sentences.en: So on the clinical side, I'd argue that there's something to be said about wearing helmets.
sentences.zh: 所以在临床方面，我认为佩戴头盔是有一定道理的。

sentences.en: But it's also just about the sport itself.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也关乎运动本身。

sentences.en: It's the risk is embedded in the style of play.
sentences.zh: 风险是植根于比赛风格之中的。

sentences.en: Are there other steps that could be taken to protect players?
sentences.zh: 还有其他可以采取的保护球员的措施吗？

sentences.en: For example, I was reading about the role of hydration in preventing TBI.
sentences.zh: 例如，我正在阅读关于补水在预防创伤性脑损伤中的作用。

sentences.en: What about strength training?
sentences.zh: 力量训练怎么样？

sentences.en: And what kind of training do coaches need that maybe they're not getting right now?
sentences.zh: 教练需要什么样的培训，而他们目前可能还没有得到？

sentences.en: It's so key.
sentences.zh: 这非常关键。

sentences.en: It's so key.

sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，我们有两项非常令人兴奋、完全由利益相关者主导的立法。

sentences.en: One, to screen everyone in the Department of Corrections for brain injury.
sentences.zh: 一项是筛查惩教署内的所有人是否有脑损伤。

sentences.en: The other woman who had a history of violent relationships who wanted to be sure that no one went through what she did.
sentences.zh: 另一位有暴力关系史的女性，她想确保没有人经历过她所经历的一切。

sentences.en: So her bill is to screen all victims of violent crime for brain injury.
sentences.zh: 所以她的法案是筛查所有暴力犯罪受害者是否有脑损伤。

sentences.en: And that's really a game-changer because then we could deliver care aimed at treating the actual brain injury, not all of the fallout of the brain injury.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个游戏规则的改变者，因为这样我们就可以提供旨在治疗实际脑损伤的护理，而不是治疗脑损伤带来的所有后果。

sentences.en: What is exciting, though, on that stakeholder side, is to see the ways that this conversation is changing the way stakeholders talk about themselves
sentences.zh: 不过，在利益相关者方面令人兴奋的是，看到这种对话正在改变利益相关者谈论自身的方式，

sentences.en: and what they want from providers and their expectations for care.
sentences.zh: 以及他们对医疗服务提供者的要求和对护理的期望。

sentences.en: And this is true on the VA side and among military and service personnel.
sentences.zh: 这在退伍军人事务部以及军人和现役人员中都是如此。

sentences.en: It's true for us in criminal justice.
sentences.zh: 这对我们刑事司法领域的人来说也是如此。

sentences.en: And it is really exciting to see communities talking about brain health in ways that are empowering and destigmatizing.
sentences.zh: 看到社区以一种赋权和去污名化的方式谈论大脑健康，这真的很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: I've got a colleague here in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 我在科罗拉多州有一位同事。

sentences.en: His work is in a new book by my colleague, Annie Leontis.
sentences.zh: 他的工作被我的同事 Annie Leontis 写进了一本新书中。

sentences.en: It's called Sex with a Brain Injury, the best ever first-person account of recovery from a brain injury
sentences.zh: 书名叫《脑损伤后的性生活》，这是有史以来关于脑损伤康复最好的第一人称叙述，

sentences.en: that has a really adept through line with historical figures from Harriet Tubman and all the presidents whose names you'll recognize.
sentences.zh: 书中巧妙地贯穿了从哈丽特·塔布曼到你所熟知的历任总统等历史人物。

sentences.en: In any case, this colleague of mine here in Colorado has really started a horror community revolution.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我在科罗拉多州的这位同事确实发起了一场社区革命。

sentences.en: And what he found is that by talking about brain health and history of brain injury,
sentences.zh: 他发现，通过谈论大脑健康和脑损伤病史，

sentences.en: it was a way to address unmet need for treatment for mental illness and treatment for historical trauma.
sentences.zh: 这成为了一种解决未满足的精神疾病治疗需求和历史创伤治疗需求的方法。

sentences.en: And it was less shaming.
sentences.zh: 而且这种方式带来的羞耻感更少。

sentences.en: And it's gotten community members to the table.
sentences.zh: 它让社区成员参与了进来。

sentences.en: And we've deployed counselors to neighborhoods that have been understandably mistrustful of psychology.
sentences.zh: 我们已经向那些对心理学怀有可以理解的怀疑态度的社区派遣了咨询师。

sentences.en: And it's really been a beautiful thing to see people take ownership of brain health and to recognize how high those stakes are.
sentences.zh: 看到人们开始掌控自己的大脑健康并认识到这些利害关系有多高，这真是一件美好的事情。

sentences.en: And we realize also that untreated brain injury makes inflammation worse.
sentences.zh: 我们也意识到，未经治疗的脑损伤会加重炎症。

sentences.en: And untreated mental illness can also aggravate inflammation.
sentences.zh: 而未经治疗的精神疾病也会加重炎症。

sentences.en: And, you know, in that way, it's a really destructive cycle.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从这个角度来看，这是一个非常具有破坏性的循环。

sentences.en: So I've been really proud to see stakeholders intervene to Tobago in ways that psychology maybe has fallen short.
sentences.zh: 所以我很自豪地看到利益相关者以心理学可能有所欠缺的方式进行干预。

sentences.en: And we could learn a lot from them.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从他们身上学到很多东西。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Gorgens, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 好的，Gorgens 博士，这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I want to thank you for spending time with me today.
sentences.zh: 我想感谢你今天花时间陪我。

sentences.en: Kim, this has been a highlight.
sentences.zh: Kim，这是一次非常精彩的对话。

sentences.en: I so appreciate you.
sentences.zh: 我非常感谢你。

sentences.en: And thanks for the invite.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你的邀请。

sentences.en: And if people need any more info where I can be helpful, they can find me here at the University of Denver.
sentences.zh: 如果人们需要更多信息或我能提供帮助的地方，他们可以在丹佛大学找到我。

sentences.en: They can find me at APA.
sentences.zh: 他们也可以在心理学协会（APA）找到我。

sentences.en: And I just really appreciate the airtime.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感谢这次交流的机会。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Spotify、YouTube 或任何你获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢你所听到的内容，请订阅并给我们留下评论。

sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由 Lee Weinerman 制作。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听。
